newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-CHILAVERT SCORES AS ARGENTINA, PARAGUAY DRAW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CHILAVERT SCORES AS ARGENTINA, PARAGUAY DRAW.

text.p: Paraguay goalkeeper Jose Luis Chilavert, playing against the team he loves to hate, scored his first goal of the Copa America as his side drew 1-1 with Argentina on Tuesday.
It was the second time in a row that the Paraguay goalkeeper has scored in a match between the two countries.
The result in group A put Argentina into the quarter-finals and means Paraguay must wait for the other two groups to finish to see if they go through as one of the two best third-placed teams.

In an eventful game between bitter rivals, Chilavert fired Paraguay in front from a 73rd minute penalty, but Argentina equalised in the last minute when Marcelo Gallardo, who had earlier missed a penalty, made good on his second chance.
Paraguay, who had a 13-month unbeaten streak snapped when they lost to Ecuador on Saturday, had slightly the better of the first half. But the real drama began after the break.

Chilavert, strangely subdued early on when he looked unsteady and was booked for dissent, had two attempts at his trademark free kicks but the first deflected off the wall and the second was saved by Carlos Roa.
Argentina were awarded a penalty in the 55th minute but Gallardo, possibly psyched out by the intimidating figure of Chilavert, fired his effort high and wide of the target.
Chilavert, who spread his arms wide and jumped up and down on the line to make the goal look smaller, celebrated aggresively as the ball flew wide.
He then showed Gallardo how a penalty should be taken, sending Roa the wrong way in the 73rd minute.
But Gallardo had the last laugh in the dying seconds, this time blasting his shot into the roof of the net in the game's third penalty.
Argentina's Pablo Rotchen was sent off for clashing with the burly Paraguay goalkeeper, having earlier been booked.
Chilavert, who regularly scores from free kicks and penalties, had not enjoyed the best of tournaments before Tuesday.
But he clearly relishes matches against Argentina, the country where he plays his club soccer for Velez Sarsfield.
On the last occasion the teams met, in a World Cup qualifier last year, Chilavert silenced the River Plate stadium in Buenos Aires when he scored from a free kick to give his country a 1-1 draw.
However, he will miss the return clash in Asuncion next month through suspension.
Ecuador were the surprise winners of the group, finishing with seven points, while Argentina were second on five and Paraguay third on four.

Argentina - 19-Carlos Roa, 21-Nelson Vivas, 20-Pablo Rotchen, 22-Gustavo Zapata, 16-Mauricio Pellegrino, 5-Rodolfo Cardozo (3-Sergio Berti, 69), 8-Marcelo Delgado, 9-Marcelo Gallardo, 1-Cristian Bassedas (18-Martin Posse, 80), 6-Raul Cardozo, 4-Jose Luis Calderon (7-Julio Cruz, 55)
